title: Acceptance criteria for repairable structured-output handshake, error taxonomy, and streaming tool-call recovery
creator: Maya Chen
description: Clarify and formalize acceptance criteria for structured output + tool/function calling when model responses are streamed and may be partial or malformed. This ticket defines an explicit error taxonomy, repairable handshake semantics (resume tokens/checkpoints), deterministic idempotent tool invocation requirements, and the expected client/console behavior under backpressure, tool timeouts, and schema drift.
background: Multiple PM and ENG discussions have highlighted ambiguity in how the runtime and clients should behave when streamed structured frames are incomplete, when tool invocations time out, or when the model emits a schema mismatch mid-stream. Existing acceptance docs cover general tool-call contracts, but we lack a single canonical checklist covering repair/retry semantics, resume tokens, and telemetry signals required for rollouts and SLOs.
proposed_solution: Define a compact error taxonomy and required frames that the runtime will emit for streamed structured outputs. Require a minimal resume token schema for in-flight streams to allow deterministic replay or graceful degradation. Introduce a deterministic tool-call idempotency contract: tool_call_id + ordered arg hash + call signature. Update SDKs to surface errors and resume tokens to clients and the Console to surface actionable diagnostics. Provide QA harness and integration tests to validate behavior across kernel restarts, network interruption, and tool failures.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Error taxonomy defined and documented: accepted codes include SCHEMA_MISMATCH, PARTIAL_EMIT, TOOL_TIMEOUT, TOOL_ERROR, TOOL_RETRY_EXHAUSTED, BACKPRESSURE_DROP, CHECKPOINT_EXPIRED. Each code has a precise meaning and suggested client-side remediation (retry with resume token, fallback to text, surface UI error, forward to human).

2) Stream frames: runtime emits structured control frames interleaved with data frames. Required control frames: STREAM_START (id, model, client_version), CHECKPOINT (cursor, resume_token), STREAM_END (status_code, summary), and TOOL_FRAME (tool_call_id, status, result_or_error). All frames must be newline-delimited JSON objects per current streaming protocol.

3) Resume token semantics: CHECKPOINT.resume_token is opaque to clients but treated as a stable handle for deterministic replay for up to 10 minutes by default. Resume must guarantee idempotent re-emission of remaining tokens without duplication when used with the same request id.

4) Tool invocation contract: every tool call in-stream must include tool_call_id and arg_hash. If the tool returns success, runtime emits TOOL_FRAME with status: SUCCESS and payload. On transient tool timeout, runtime emits TOOL_FRAME with status: TOOL_TIMEOUT and an automatic retry will be attempted up to N (configurable, default 1). Retries must use the same tool_call_id to ensure idempotency.

5) Client SDK behavior: when encountering CHECKPOINT with resume_token, SDK should persist resume_token in memory and expose an API to resume with the same request_id. When SCHEMA_MISMATCH is received mid-stream, SDK should: a) surface a SchemaMismatch exception with the offending frame and suggested action, b) if resume_token present, optionally request a replay with stricter validation flags.

6) Backward compatibility: older clients that do not understand control frames must continue to receive concatenated textual output without protocol-breaking characters. Runtime must include a compatibility flag on STREAM_START to allow fallback plain-text emission for legacy clients.

7) Tests: unit tests for frame parsing, integration tests that simulate: tool timeouts, partial emission mid-stream, resume token replay, and schema drift. Acceptance requires zero flaky tests > 1% across 50 runs in CI.

8) Metrics and thresholds: emit telemetry events: stream_start, checkpoint_emitted, tool_call_initiated, tool_call_completed, tool_call_failed, schema_mismatch, resume_attempt, resume_success. Console dashboards must show 95th-percentile time-to-recovery for resume and a regression alert if schema_mismatch rate increases by >50% week-over-week or absolute >0.5% of streams.

9) Rollout gating: feature gated behind runtime flag. Block rollout if tool_call_id collisions observed in telemetry or if resume_replay_success_rate < 99% on canary traffic.

10) Documentation and examples: PRD includes minimal examples of a successful streaming tool-handshake, a replay flow, and an error flow. SDK docs updated with code snippets for resuming and handling schema_mismatch.
out_of_scope:
- Full redesign of the streaming wire protocol (we only add control frames within existing newline-delimited JSON streaming).
- Implementing custom per-tenant retry policies (handled by Dedicated/Private ops).
- Building alternate UI surfaces beyond Console telemetry (non-critical).
testing_plan:
- Unit tests: parser + control frame validator.
- Integration: end-to-end harness that runs model->runtime->mock-tool->SDK client; scenarios include network drops, tool crash, kernel restart.
- Chaos tests: random drop of final CHECKPOINT frames at 1%, 5%.
- Regression: run existing structured-output acceptance suite and new resume tests on each PR.
- QA checklist: manual exploratory for edge-cases (concurrent tool calls, large payloads >1MB, slow consumer backpressure).
rollout_plan: 1) Implement feature flag in runtime. 2) Ship SDK changes behind flag. 3) Canary with internal customers for 2 weeks and monitor telemetry. 4) Progressive rollout to 10%/50%/100% with automatic rollback if block gates trigger. 5) Announce migration notes to external customers and provide compatibility knob.
monitoring_and_telemetry:
Required telemetry events and sample attributes: 
- stream_start: request_id, model, client_version, is_compat_mode
- checkpoint_emitted: request_id, cursor, resume_token_hash
- tool_call_initiated: tool_call_id, arg_hash, request_id
- tool_call_completed: tool_call_id, latency_ms, success
- tool_call_failed: tool_call_id, error_code, retry_count
- schema_mismatch: request_id, frame_index, expected_schema_hash
- resume_attempt: request_id, resume_token_age_ms, result(success|fail)
Dashboards: resume_success_rate (by model, by region), schema_mismatch_rate, avg_time-to-replay, tool_retry_rate. Alert thresholds defined in acceptance criteria.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Resume tokens leak sensitive info. Mitigation: tokens are opaque, short-lived, and hashed in telemetry.
- Risk: Idempotency violations cause duplicate tool effects. Mitigation: require tool_call_id + arg_hash; runtime rejects ambiguous retries and returns TOOL_RETRY_EXHAUSTED.
- Risk: Increased runtime complexity leads to regressions. Mitigation: gated rollout, canary tests, and automated chaos tests.
- Risk: Legacy clients break. Mitigation: compatibility flag and explicit backward-compat mode during rollout.
